sentences.zh: 安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔是儿童图书管理员的负责人

sentences.en: at the New York Public Library
sentences.zh: 在纽约公共图书馆

sentences.en: for pretty much the whole first half of the 20th century.

sentences.zh: 在近三十年的时间里，

sentences.zh: 在终于给她拍下照片的时候，

sentences.en: she was an older lady who looked like the quintessential bun-in-the-hair,
sentences.zh: 她是一位老妇人，看起来像典型的盘头、

sentences.zh: 喜欢嘘人的图书管理员，是一个很容易扮演的反派。

sentences.en: But as Dan would find out, Moore was and remains a very complicated historical figure.
sentences.zh: 但正如丹所发现的那样，摩尔过去是、现在仍然是一个非常复杂的历史人物。

sentences.en: Because long before she became a villainous banner of books,
sentences.zh: 因为早在她成为图书禁令的反派旗手之前，

sentences.en: Anne Carroll Moore was a hero of children's literature
sentences.zh: 安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔就是儿童文学的英雄

sentences.en: who left the world with one undeniably good thing.
sentences.zh: 她给世界留下了无可争议的好东西。

sentences.en: She pretty much single-handedly invented the children's library.
sentences.zh: 她几乎单枪匹马地发明了儿童图书馆。

sentences.en: Jill Lepore is a professor of history at Harvard
sentences.zh: 吉尔·莱波雷是哈佛大学的历史学教授

sentences.en: and a staff writer for The New Yorker who wrote about more for the magazine.
sentences.zh: 也是《纽约客》的特约撰稿人，她曾为该杂志撰写过关于摩尔的文章。

sentences.en: And she says that perhaps no single person has ever done more
sentences.zh: 她说，也许从来没有人做过更多的努力

sentences.en: to get books into the hands of children.
sentences.zh: 把书送到孩子们手中。

sentences.en: And she did so by creating a place for kids to read.
sentences.zh: 她通过为孩子们创造一个阅读空间做到了这一点。

sentences.en: So when you go into your neighborhood public library
sentences.zh: 所以当你走进你那里的社区公共图书馆

sentences.zh: 有一个叫儿童阅览室的地方

sentences.en: and they have toys
sentences.zh: 他们有玩具

sentences.en: and they have a cozy rug and a rocking chair
sentences.zh: 他们有一张舒适的地毯和一个摇椅

sentences.en: and they have story hours
sentences.zh: 他们有故事时间

sentences.en: and they have fun art on the walls.
sentences.zh: 墙上还有有趣的艺术品。

sentences.en: Like all that stuff was invented by Anne Carroll Moore.
sentences.zh: 就像所有这些东西都是安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔发明的一样。

sentences.en: Today, with all the emphasis we place
sentences.zh: 今天，随着我们所有的强调

sentences.en: on instilling kids with a love of reading,
sentences.zh: 在向孩子们灌输对阅读的热爱上，

sentences.en: it's hard to imagine your local public library
sentences.zh: 很难想象你当地的公共图书馆

sentences.en: without a children's reading room.
sentences.zh: 没有儿童阅览室。

sentences.en: But Lepore says that before Moore came along,
sentences.zh: 但莱波雷说，在摩尔出现之前，

sentences.en: Children weren't even allowed to enter the one place they would be sure to find a book.
sentences.zh: 孩子们甚至不被允许进入那个他们肯定能找到书的地方。

sentences.en: Kids really couldn't go to libraries.
sentences.zh: 孩子们真的不能去图书馆。

sentences.en: Libraries were for grown-ups.
sentences.zh: 图书馆是给成年人准备的。

sentences.en: The late 19th century saw some of the first public libraries being built in America.
sentences.zh: 19世纪末，美国建造了第一批公共图书馆。

sentences.en: This was an age in which there was a surge in support for government-funded, progressive institutions intended for the betterment of all.
sentences.zh: 这是一个对政府资助的、旨在造福所有人的进步机构的支持激增的时代。

sentences.en: Or, in the case of libraries, the betterment of everyone except children.
sentences.zh: 或者，就图书馆而言，是为了造福除儿童以外的所有人。

sentences.en: You had to be, I think, 14 or 16 in most places, and in most places you had to be a boy.
sentences.zh: 我想在大多数地方你必须14岁或16岁，而且在大多数地方你必须是个男孩。

sentences.en: And the Brooklyn public schools had a policy that children below the third grade do not read well enough to profit from the use of library books.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克林公立学校有一项政策，即三年级以下的儿童阅读能力不足以从使用图书馆书籍中受益。

sentences.en: The thinking went that if you were too young to read, obviously there would be no need for you to go to the library.
sentences.zh: 当时的观点是，如果你太小而不会读书，显然你没有必要去图书馆。

sentences.en: What good would that do you?
sentences.zh: 那对你有什么好处？

sentences.en: And if you were old enough to read but you were still a child, going into a library which was full of trashy romance novels and westerns would just corrupt your mind.
sentences.zh: 如果你到了读书的年龄但你仍然是个孩子，走进一个充满低俗言情小说和西部片的图书馆只会败坏你的心智。

sentences.en: And so certainly there's no reason for you to go to a library either.
sentences.zh: 所以当然你也没有理由去图书馆。

sentences.en: Jill Lepore says that for the children of the wealthy and middle classes, who often had their own small book collections at home,
sentences.zh: 吉尔·莱波雷说，对于富裕和中产阶级家庭的孩子来说，他们家里往往有自己的小藏书，

sentences.en: being banned from libraries wasn't really a problem.
sentences.zh: 被禁止进入图书馆并不是什么真正的问题。

sentences.en: But it left the children of the poor with virtually no access to literature.
sentences.zh: 但这让穷人的孩子实际上无法接触到文学。

sentences.en: It's completely bound up with class discrimination, right?
sentences.zh: 这完全与阶级歧视挂钩，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's not really until the 1920s that you have a very strict regulation against child labor.
sentences.zh: 因为直到20世纪20年代，你才对童工有非常严格的规定。

sentences.en: So the children of the poor are working.
sentences.zh: 所以穷人的孩子都在工作。

sentences.en: Like, they're not reading.
sentences.zh: 就像，他们不读书。

sentences.en: They're not even learning to read.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至没有学习阅读。

sentences.en: But then, at the turn of the century, Anne Carroll Moore,
sentences.zh: 但随后，在世纪之交，安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔，

sentences.zh: 那个讨厌《晚安，月亮》的脾气暴躁的老图书管理员，

sentences.en: came along and flipped the purpose of the library on its head.
sentences.zh: 出现并彻底颠覆了图书馆的宗旨。

sentences.zh: 所以我最近在阅读一篇文章时感到非常惊讶

sentences.en: someone described her as the quintessential librarian
sentences.zh: 有人将她描述为典型的图书管理员

sentences.en: with the bun in her hair and shushing the children
sentences.zh: 盘着头发，对孩子们嘘声制止

sentences.zh: 然而事实上，这正是她没有做的事情。

sentences.en: Jan Pinborough is an editor and children's book author,
sentences.zh: 简·平伯勒是一名编辑兼儿童图书作家，

sentences.en: and she says that in the 1890s,
sentences.zh: 她说在19世纪90年代，

sentences.en: Moore was the most vocal and energetic
sentences.zh: 摩尔是最直言不讳、充满活力的人

sentences.en: among a small group of young progressive librarians
sentences.zh: 在一小群年轻的进步图书管理员中

sentences.en: who had begun experimenting with a radical idea.
sentences.zh: 他们开始尝试一个激进的想法。

sentences.zh: 如果他们终于让孩子们进入图书馆，

sentences.zh: 在某个区域备满儿童读物，

sentences.zh: 然后把那个区域只留给孩子们呢？

sentences.zh: 而她正试图做的是，

sentences.en: and this is what's really important,
sentences.zh: 这也是非常重要的，

sentences.zh: 她正试图为工人阶级的孩子提供一个童年。

sentences.zh: 她正试图拉平这个领域。

sentences.zh: 1906年，摩尔获得了在空前规模上进行这项实验的机会。

sentences.zh: 纽约公共图书馆正在建造其标志性的总馆

sentences.zh: 位于42街和第五大道的转角处。

sentences.zh: 它将设有一个专门的儿童阅览室

sentences.zh: 该阅览室将由摩尔设计、备货和运营。

sentences.zh: 那里有一些令人难以置信的照片，记录了那个儿童阅览室

sentences.zh: 当它在1911年开业时。

sentences.zh: 摩尔首先借鉴了儿童尺寸的桌椅的想法

sentences.en: from kindergartens.
sentences.zh: 来自幼儿园。

sentences.zh: 但她将这个概念推得更远。

sentences.zh: 她有长椅，窗户座椅建在

sentences.zh: 摩尔特别想要

sentences.zh: 让来自贫民窟的贫穷孩子接触到自然世界的美丽。

sentences.zh: 所以她安装了

sentences.zh: 粉红色的地砖来捕捉穿过窗户的光线，然后用贝壳

sentences.zh: 收藏品、蝴蝶和几十碗新鲜切好的花朵填满整个房间。

sentences.en: And these children, a lot of
sentences.zh: 而这些孩子中，有很大一部分

sentences.zh: 极度渴望接触大自然，每当她把花拿进屋里时

sentences.en: when she brought them in.
sentences.zh: 他们就会排着队去欣赏和闻一闻花香。

sentences.zh: 摩尔取下了那些冷冰冰的标志。

sentences.zh: 图书馆如今变成了一个空间

sentences.zh: 用来举办木偶戏、音乐表演和故事时间，并提供多种语言的故事，

sentences.en: And by some point, according to Jill Lepore, the whole conceit was taken so far that Nicholas actually had his own letterhead.

sentences.en: Because it was just understood that Moore and Nicholas were like a package deal.
sentences.zh: 因为大家心照不宣，摩尔和尼古拉斯就像是一个捆绑组合。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.

sentences.en: But, you know, despite the creep factor, keep in mind that, like, you know, kids also wrote to Nicholas, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，尽管有点让人毛骨悚然，但请记住，孩子们也会写信给尼古拉斯，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.

sentences.en: And some of the correspondence and gifts Nicholas received from adults also suggests that a lot of people saw Nicholas as this benign or even kind of benevolent presence.
sentences.zh: 而且尼古拉斯从成年人那里收到的一些信件和礼物也表明，很多人将尼古拉斯视为一种良性的甚至可以说是仁慈的存在。

sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，《三只山羊嘎啦嘎啦》的作者为安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔制作了她第一本书的微缩版，供尼古拉斯随身携带。

sentences.en: Beatrix Potter sent her these little hand-drawn postcards depicting Peter Rabbit and Nicholas together, almost as if they were friends.
sentences.zh: 碧翠丝·波特寄给她这些手绘的小明信片，上面描绘了彼得兔和尼古拉斯在一起，简直就像朋友一样。

sentences.en: And according to Jan, one of the employees from the library was like this Russian emigre, and she apparently gave Nicholas like a Fabergé egg.
sentences.zh: 据简说，图书馆的一名员工是个俄罗斯移民，她显然送给尼古拉斯一颗法贝热彩蛋。

sentences.en: Whoa, like a real Fabergé with like gemstones in it type of Fabergé egg.
sentences.zh: 哇，就像那种镶有宝石的真正的法贝热彩蛋。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, she said there was a gem inside.
sentences.zh: 对，好吧，她说里面有一颗宝石。

sentences.en: So I'm going to go with at least a, yes, a Fabergé egg with one gem.
sentences.zh: 所以我倾向于认为至少有，对，一颗镶有一颗宝石的法贝热彩蛋。

sentences.en: But the point is, is that in the end, you can make an argument that Nicholas Knickerbocker's reign in the balance, you know, did more good than harm.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，到头来，你可以说尼古拉斯·尼克尔伯克在天平上的统治，你知道的，利大于弊。

sentences.en: And as was so much of what Anne Carole Moore did, it's a close call.
sentences.zh: 就像安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔所做的很多事情一样，这是一个微妙的判断。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, creating a character to make kids comfortable in the library is a totally nice and joyful thing to do.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，创造一个角色让孩子们在图书馆感到舒适是一件非常美好和快乐的事。

sentences.en: But, you know, I hope it was good on balance.
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道，我希望总的来说它是好的。

sentences.en: I mean, I hope for everyone's sake it was good on balance.

sentences.zh: 所以尼古拉斯·尼克尔伯克，作为安妮·卡罗尔·摩尔人格的延伸，
